request.spec:
A button on each person's row downloads their row as a CSV file: a header line cell,value then one
line per cell for person-name, person-grade, person-claimed, person-due-total, person-statement-count,
person-overdue-total, person-hold, person-retired, person-aliases and person-score, in that order,
each with the value as the row shows it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button on each person's row downloads their row as a CSV file: a header line cell,value then one
line per cell for person-name, person-grade, person-claimed, person-due-total, person-statement-count,
person-overdue-total, person-hold, person-retired, person-aliases and person-score, in that order,
each with the value as the row shows it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now has an "Export (CSV)" button (`data-testid="person-export"`), and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

When you press it, the file starts with the line `cell,value`, then has one line for each of the ten cells in the order you asked for. It waits until the sheet has finished reloading its data, then copies each value straight from the row as it's displayed. That means it matches what's on screen, including while an as-of or preview date is set. Values containing a comma or quote are quoted, like `"Lee, Jo (B)"`.

One thing to know: if a user has hidden one of those columns, that cell's line is still in the file but its value is empty. I chose this so the file only ever holds what the row shows. The other option would be to recalculate hidden values separately.

It's a front-end change only, with no server or stored-data changes and no audit records. The new code is in `src/main/frontend/features/export/personexport.slot.tsx` and reuses the existing CSV helpers in `features/export/csv.ts`. The button has its own column at the end of the people table, after the timeline column.
